results.separate_actual_example: The inverse-verified example187 realizes the DIFFERENT common-factor relation (X^2 Z+XYW-Y^4), already recognized186. The polynomial maps through (X,Y,I,J) have both inverse orders; literal partial_Z gives N=partial_y, and a fraction-field plus irreducibility argument proves the full initial kernel. It starts with A=C[y,t,rho] and a translation slice, so proves nonvacuity of that restricted configuration, not a new recognition theorem or globally minimal time profile.
results.zero_R187: For R=k_rho=0, the constant-y determinant forces n_rho=theta_v=0 and C0=-ell_rho nonzero. The actual field intersection L=C(y,z) yields original partial_W commuting with E. Primitive Wang classification and the t^4 versus quadratic leading coefficient exclude this case. Nonconstant y then has s=n_rho nonzero, theta=P(y) of degree three, w=W(y) of degree at most six, and L[y]=L[v]. The exact scalar equations retain gamma=Ny and force (s^-2)_rhorho=0 and rho=A_c*n^2/2+B_c*n+C_c over K, without yet L=K(n).
results.nonzero_R188: For R nonzero, it is a field scalar, so the first potential gives L[y,theta]=L[v]. The actual cleared R^2 J identity proves a nonzero eliminant and unit evaluated cofactor. If R_rho is nonzero, its quartic top has distinct multiplicities(3,1). A proved one-point-at-infinity statement and all factor-degree cases force y constant. Thus nonconstant y implies R_rho=0.
results.constant_projection188: Constant y with R nonzero is excluded separately. The actual LND P=aN-(NX)E fixes X,Y and commutes with E. Invariant primitive division preserves these gates. Published two-variable triangularity and the time-leading relation force affine coefficients B0,C0. A unit ideal gives an explicit coordinate inverse; independent nonunit affine coefficients give only a polynomial kernel by contraction. Wang on that actual three-ring contradicts the leading rho or t^4 coefficient in every case. Primitive gcd is not treated as a unit ideal.
results.cover_collapse189: In the zero-R branch, exact recurrences make P,W polynomial in n over K. Actual function-field return then proves L=K(n). A proved polynomial-pencil pole-degree bound forces any nonconstant leading coefficient gamma of w as a polynomial in z to generate K. The genuine quadratic cover gives gamma^2*t^9 constant nonzero; a nonconstant linear slope gives gamma^2*t^7 constant nonzero. Integer valuation at gamma=0 excludes both. Hence rho=b*n+c, b in C*, c in K, and n_rho=1/b. K is not assumed rational.
results.quartic_graph189: In the nonzero-R branch, the V-degree bound gives degree(y) at most two. Vanishing quartic top has mixed cubic multiplicities and is excluded without rejecting algebraic fourth-root coefficients. The exhaustive affine and nested-quadratic cases reduce either to a pure quartic graph or to a square-completion ODE. A local finite-ramification Laurent proof shows every nonzero algebraic solution of (f+4tf')f'''-3f'f''-3t(f'')^2=0 is affine, including all possible tails. Thus y is affine, theta=P(y) has degree four, R=1/(A*t+B), and n=C*R^2*rho+n0, with A,B,C complex and k0,n0 in K; A=0 and C=0 are allowed.
results.combined_scope: Every supplied absent-variable chart considered here has affine generic y. The zero-R branch is an exact cubic graph with a constant-slope linear coefficient cover; the nonzero-R branch is a quartic graph with reciprocal-linear R. These are coefficient-field reductions, not an original-ring polynomial coordinate, a recognition theorem for this absent-variable form, or unrestricted cancellation.
